meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: South Korea (Republic of Korea) - Unitary National Commercial Registry Jurisdiction for Yuhan Hoesa

Free Trade Agreement between the Government of the Republic of Korea and the Government of the People's Republic of China (Korea-China FTA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information (FTRA), as amended; Act on Regulation and Punishment of Criminal Proceeds Concealment, as amended; Act on Prohibition of Financing of Public Menace and Weapons of Mass Destruction Proliferation, as amended; Real Name Financial Transactions Act, as amended; Commercial Act, as amended, Articles 262-269 and 279 (Yuhan Hoesa); Enforcement Decree of the Commercial Act; Financial Services Commission and Financial Intelligence Unit regulations on customer due diligence and beneficial ownership reporting; FATF Recommendations 24 and 25. The Yuhan Hoesa beneficial owner(s) must be filed with the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit and the competent court/registry on a Government-only-access basis; there is no public UBO register.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registrar / companies registry of the shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the issuing state is a Hague Apostille Convention state: notarize the certified extract, obtain a 1961 Hague Apostille from the designated competent authority, and submit directly without consular legalization. If the issuing state is not an Apostille Convention state: notarize, authenticate at the home-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalize at the Republic of Korea Embassy or Consulate. These two paths are parallel alternatives and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign company registrar or official corporate register in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention state path: notarize, obtain Apostille, no Korean consular legalization. Non-Apostille state path: notarize, home-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, Korean Embassy/Consulate consular legalization. Parallel paths; do not combine.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing the Korean Yuhan Hoesa incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign corporate shareholder(s), notarized
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention state path: notarize, Apostille, direct filing. Non-Apostille state path: notarize, home-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Korean consular legalization. Parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (foreign shareholder constitutive documents plus proposed Korean-language Yuhan Hoesa Articles of Association)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate registry for the shareholder's articles; a Korean notary public for the proposed Yuhan Hoesa articles
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Foreign shareholder articles: Apostille state path uses notarization and Apostille only; non-Apostille state path uses notarization, home-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and Korean consular legalization. Korean Yuhan Hoesa articles are notarized by a Korean notary public and do not require any foreign authentication.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the investor's relationship bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The issuing bank head office or branch, signed under a bank officer's title
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille state path: notarize the banker's signature, Apostille, direct submission. Non-Apostille state path: notarize, home-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Korean Embassy/Consulate legalization. The two paths are alternatives; do not apply consecutively.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO identification documents (passport, Directors and Officers identification, and Foreign Resident Registration where applicable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority of the UBO's country of nationality and the relevant alien/resident authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille state path: notarize the document copy, Apostille, no Korean consular legalization. Non-Apostille state path: notarize, home-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Korean consular legalization. Parallel paths only.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, officers, signatories, vessel masters, counterparty enterprises, charterers, and bunker suppliers must be screened before incorporation and on a continuing basis. The mandatory protocol includes OFAC SDN and OFAC consolidated screening; UN Security Council Consolidated List and all applicable UN sanctions resolutions; Korean FSC/FIU designated individuals and organizations; the Korean Foreign Exchange Transactions Act restricted-party lists; EU and UK HM Treasury financial sanctions lists; domestic and foreign PEP databases covering Korean public officials, senior foreign politicians, heads of state, ministers, and close associates; adverse-media review; vessel IMO number and flag-state checks; and cross-referencing of corporate identifiers, aliases, addresses, and beneficial owner data against sanctions and PEP typologies. Any hit triggers Enhanced Due Diligence, senior partner approval, and, where required, automatic Suspicious Transaction Report filing to the Korean FIU under FTRA.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IRO) - official Korean court registry online service for trade-name search and name reservation; physical filing at the District Court with jurisdiction over the registered office
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Every Korean corporate trade name must be registrable in the Korean alphabet (Hangul); a foreign-language name may be used only as a phonetic transliteration into Hangul. The registered name must close with the legal form suffix 'Yuhan Hoesa'. The four-tier naming convention requires: (1) a distinctive element identifying the enterprise; (2) a descriptive business-purpose element limited to bunkering, ship supply, lubricant replenishment, and ancillary marine services; (3) the statutory 'Yuhan Hoesa' legal-form suffix; and (4) if a Latin-script equivalent appears on invoices or bank instructions, the romanization must exactly match the registered Hangul name and may not create a new legal form or translation inconsistent with the Korean registration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 14 days of receiving the registry's written refusal, the applicant may file a corrective application at the same district registry addressing each stated ground of rejection, including name similarity, prohibited token, missing Yuhan Hoesa suffix, invalid Hangul transliteration, or business-purpose mismatch. The registry officer must re-review the corrected application. If the refusal is maintained, the applicant may file an immediate appeal to the High Court within 7 days of the refusal notification. The appeal brief must state the original application date, the impugned decision, corrected trade name, and a memorandum on non-confusion with existing registered names. If the appeal fails, the applicant must file a new reservation containing a new distinctive element because an expired or finally rejected reservation cannot be revived.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Rejected for this industry. For ISIC 5222 offshore bunkering and refueling, a virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible. The Korean Petroleum and Petroleum Substitute Fuel Business Act, the Harbor Act, and the Act on Registration of Business require a real fixed place of business in Korea with physical presence, responsible managerial staff, bunkering and port permits, environmental compliance files, and terminal access arrangements. The National Tax Service validates the actual place of business during business registration, and banks opening the Yuhan Hoesa operating account for SWIFT wires and standby letters of credit will reject a virtual-only address. A physical registered office and an operating location must be established before the incorporation filing is deemed complete.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for an unannounced physical inspection: (1) presence of a responsible employee or manager; (2) original lease contract and rent payment proof; (3) business registration certificate and tax invoices; (4) petroleum and bunkering permits, environmental certificates, and port-area licenses; (5) vessel registration, crew list, and bunker delivery logs; and (6) bank account opening documents. Quantified risk: 70% in the first 18 months for a marine bunkering entity because the National Tax Service, Korea Coast Guard, municipal port authorities, and Korean Customs routinely conduct unannounced inspections. Registry and tax officers may also re-verify any registered office address carrying a shared-office or commercial-mailbox marker.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal fee for Stage 1 due diligence, UBO piercing, name clearance, and sanctions/PEP screening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External Korean counsel (partner and AML/CFT compliance officer)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Korean market benchmark for a standard Yuhan Hoesa formation with enhanced UBO and AML due diligence; USD 2,500-4,500 excluding disbursements.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory fee for electronic name search and reservation; official court filing fee is collected only at incorporation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Korean notarization of proposed Yuhan Hoesa Articles of Association
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Local Korean notary public in the registered-office district
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notary Public Act statutory tariff for articles notarization based on stated capital; market benchmark approximately KRW 300,000 (USD 220).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Court commercial registration tax, education surcharge, and filing fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: District Court Commercial Registry and municipal education tax authorities
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Local Tax Act: 0.4% registration tax on issued capital plus 20% education surcharge and court filing fee; estimate assumes KRW 100,000,000 nominal capital (minimum capital is not legally required).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Foreign exchange inward-remittance and investment report filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Receiving foreign-exchange bank / Korean Customs and foreign-exchange reporting gateway
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Foreign Exchange Transactions Act mandatory report; bank service fee benchmark of USD 100-200.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: National Tax Service branch with jurisdiction over the registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official fee; statutory obligation under the Act on Registration of Business within 20 days of incorporation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Korean translation and notarization of foreign corporate and banking documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Korean translator and notary public
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of USD 80-120 per document for Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing, Board Resolution/PoA, Articles, and Bank Reference Letter.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization disbursements for the five-document bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Home-country competent authority issuing Hague Apostille, or Republic of Korea Embassy/Consulate for consular legalization, plus courier and government fees
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Actual government tariffs and third-party disbursements; not a lawyer fee; estimated at USD 400-900 depending on home jurisdiction.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO, PEP, and sanctions screening database subscription and per-name hit analysis
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial compliance data provider and Korean counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for one-time screening of all individuals and entities holding a 25% or more beneficial interest, including OFAC, UN, EU, UK, Korean FIU, and global PEP sources.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Physical registered office and operating-site setup for the required actual place of business
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Landlord and building management at a commercial office in a Korean port district
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Commercial-lease market benchmark for a six-month initial setup and first-quarter operating cost; required for National Tax Service, bank account opening, and bunkering license compliance; not a legal fee.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Part IV Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa), Articles 543 through 613; Article 635 (registration); Article 39 (act of contribution); Value-Added Tax Act Article 8 (business registration).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Court Registration Office of the Seoul Central District Court, or the district court registration office having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office address of the Yuhan Hoesa.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa and the Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company, together with the written share subscription schedule, capital deposit certificate, minutes of the inaugural general meeting, minutes of the first board of directors meeting, and written consents and oaths of the directors and auditor.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Commercial Act does not impose any minimum paid-up capital requirement for a Yuhan Hoesa and there is no statutory blocked escrow account rule. Directors are, however, required to deposit the total subscribed contributions with a licensed bank and obtain a capital deposit certificate, which must be presented to the court registry. If a marine bunkering license under the Harbor Transport Business Act is pursued, the applicant may be asked to demonstrate financial solvency, operational assurance capacity, and oil pollution liability insurance.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF DIRECTORS OF YUHAN HOESA

Pursuant to a unanimous written consent of the first board of directors of Yuhan Hoesa (the Company), a limited liability company formed under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, at a meeting duly convened and held, the following resolutions were adopted:

1. Corporate Capital and Share Subscription. RESOLVED that the initial subscribed capital of the Company be and is hereby approved in the amount stated in the Articles of Incorporation; that all allottees shown in the subscription schedule are deemed to have subscribed to the shares set opposite their respective names; and that the board accepts such subscriptions, allocates the shares, and applies the contributions to the registered capital of the Company.

2. Registered Office Adoption. RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be and is hereby established at the address set forth in the Articles of Incorporation, Republic of Korea; that the district court registration office having territorial jurisdiction over such address is designated as the registry with which the incorporation of the Company shall be filed; that the Representative Director is authorized to execute the lease or service agreement for the registered office, to post all legally required notices, and to display the corporate trade name at such office.

3. Bank Authorization. RESOLVED that the bank designated in the bank authorization schedule, together with such other financial institutions as the Representative Director may select, is hereby appointed as the principal bank of the Company; and that the Representative Director and each person designated in the bank signature schedule are authorized, jointly with a second authorized signatory where required by the bank, to open all corporate current, savings, foreign exchange, and settlement accounts; to execute account mandates; to procure SWIFT wire facilities and standby letters of credit; to endorse checks and payment orders; and to give receipts and releases.

4. Appointment of Statutory Officers. RESOLVED that the persons named in the written consent and oath of office filed with these minutes are appointed as the first Representative Director, Director(s), and Auditor respectively, each to serve until the next ordinary general meeting of members; and that the Representative Director is fully authorized to complete all registrations, tax filings, customs permits, banking documentation, port and marine fuel supply licenses, environmental impact, civil defense, fire safety, and employment filings, to affix the corporate seal, and to appoint sub-agents for such purposes.

5. General Authority. RESOLVED that all officers and agents of the Company are authorized to take any further action, execute any certificates, affidavits, applications, and powers of attorney, and pay any fees required in order to carry out these resolutions; and that all acts performed by the promoters and the initial board before the date of these minutes are ratified and confirmed in all respects.

Adopted by unanimous vote on this [Date] day of [Month], [Year].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation and Share Subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed notary public qualified under the Korean Notarial Deeds Act; no court filing yet at this stage.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founding member must sign the Articles of Incorporation of the Yuhan Hoesa before a licensed Korean notary. The articles must set out the commercial name, the objective clause covering ship bunkering and marine fuel refueling services under ISIC 5222 and NAICS 488390, the amount of capital, the number of shares, the rights attaching to the shares, the structure of directors and auditor, the method of contribution, and the registered office address. All members must execute a share subscription schedule stating the number of shares subscribed and the amount of contribution payable in cash. The notary verifies identity, legal capacity, and legality of the corporate purpose, authenticates the signatures and corporate seal imprint, and issues the notarial certificate.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation
Member identification documents or passports
Proof of domestic address and contact details
Corporate seal or certified signature specimen
Statement of the business objective with ISIC 5222 and NAICS 488390
Certificate of foreign registration or trust deed if a corporate member is used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises a query or refuses authentication, the defect is procedural and can be cured by amending the draft articles and resubmitting the corrected document to the same notary. There is no administrative appeal before the notary stage; the correct remedy is correction and re-execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Paid-Up Contributions and Adoption of First Shareholders and Board Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A commercial bank licensed in the Republic of Korea; the inaugural general meeting of members; the first board of directors.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, the total subscribed capital must be paid in cash by transferring it to a temporary deposit account opened in the name of the company or the promoter in a recognized Korean commercial bank. The bank issues a certificate of deposit of incorporation capital. Thereafter, the promoters convene an inaugural general meeting of members at which the directors and auditor are appointed. Immediately following that meeting, the first board of directors adopts the pro-forma board resolution contained in this dossier, appoints the Representative Director, adopts the registered office, authorizes the opening of the principal bank accounts, and appoints the statutory officers. Written minutes must be executed and retained as corporate records.
required_dossiers: Certificate of deposit of incorporation capital issued by the bank
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Minutes of the inaugural general meeting of members
Signed consent and oath of office of each director and auditor
Adopted Pro-Forma First Board Resolution
Lease agreement or proof of right to use the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional anti-money-laundering documentation for the temporary capital account, the promoters must complete enhanced customer due diligence and resubmit. If the board meeting is challenged as invalid due to defective notice or consent, the cure is a written unanimous consent executed by all directors, which is valid under the Commercial Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Incorporation Registration at the Competent District Court Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Office of the Seoul Central District Court or the district court registration office with jurisdiction over the Yuhan Hoesa registered office, supervised by the National Court Administration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Representative Director must submit the Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company to the civil registration office of the competent district court. The court checks whether the submitted articles are notarized, whether the capital has been deposited, whether the statutory officers are validly appointed, and whether the trade name and object clause are registrable. Upon acceptance of all documents, the court assesses and collects the prescribed registration stamp duty and enters the company into the corporate register. The court then issues the certified certificate of registered matters, which is definitive evidence of incorporation and commencement of legal personality.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Incorporation
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Share subscription schedule
Bank certificate of capital deposit
Minutes of the inaugural general meeting
Minutes of the first board meeting and adopted resolutions
Written consent letters and seal specimens of directors and auditor
Power of attorney if filed by a licensed corporate service agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction order or refuses registration, the company must within the court stated period correct the defects, substitute documents, or supplement evidence and resubmit. An immediate appeal to the court division responsible for registration is available if the refusal is allegedly unlawful. Legal counsel can cure most errors without restarting the incorporation process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Business Registration Certificate and Tax-Office Notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea through the HomeTax online portal and the competent district tax office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following the court registration, the company must apply for a business registration certificate under Article 8 of the Value-Added Tax Act. The Representative Director logs onto HomeTax with an accredited certificate or through a licensed tax agent and files the business registration application using information drawn from the certified court registration matter. The tax office verifies the corporate identification number, registered office address, representative identity, business objective, and banking details, then issues the business registration certificate. This certificate must be obtained before the company lawfully carries on the marine bunkering business and before opening permanent VAT invoicing accounts.
required_dossiers: Certified certificate of registered matters from the court
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Representative Director identity documents
Proof of registered office address
Corporate seal certificate
Business registration application filed through the HomeTax portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office returns the application for correction, the defect is typically an address mismatch or incomplete business description; the company must promptly amend the affected item and resubmit through HomeTax. If there is disagreement with the classification of the taxable business code, an explanatory letter with the ISIC and NAICS codes can be filed and the tax office will adjust the registration within one or two business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industry Bunkering Licensing, Environmental Classification, and Fire/Civil Defense Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries (MOF), regional Maritime Affairs and Fisheries Office; local municipal fuel sales licensing department; Korea Coast Guard; National Fire Agency; Ministry of Environment.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The company must submit an application for Port Transport Business Registration for ship bunkering to the regional MOF office, together with evidence of vessel ownership or charter, a port facility lease, an oil spill response plan, and financial capability. A separate petroleum sales registration must be filed with the relevant local government under the Petroleum and Petroleum Substitute Fuel Business Act. The company must classify its environmental approval tier: vessel-only operations inside an existing port are generally exempt from full EIA, while onshore fuel storage tanks trigger Prior Environmental Review or Full EIA thresholds. Before operation, the company must obtain a fire safety completion certificate from the National Fire Agency, a KOSHA workplace safety certification, and Korea Coast Guard approval of the Oil Pollution Emergency Response Plan.
required_dossiers: Completed application forms for Port Transport Business Registration and Petroleum Sales Business Registration
Certificate of business registration and court registration
Vessel ownership or long-term charter documents for bunkering tankers or barges
Port berth or mooring facility lease
Oil Pollution Emergency Response Plan approved by the Korea Coast Guard
Fire safety completion certificate or application receipt
Environmental registration confirmation or coordinator referral notice
Proof of financial solvency and insurance coverage
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOF or the municipal authority suspends or rejects the application, the company may respond to the supplementary-data request within the stipulated period. If refusal is based on missing vessel compliance documents, charterparty amendments and class survey certificates should be filed as additional evidence. An administrative appeal may be filed with the Administrative Appeals Commission if final refusal occurs.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries (MOF), regional Maritime Affairs and Fisheries Office; local municipal government for petroleum retail licensing; Korea Coast Guard; National Fire Agency; Ministry of Environment.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Port Transport Business Registration for Ship Bunkering (Marine Fuel Supply Business) under the Harbor Transport Business Act, and Petroleum Sales Business Registration under the Petroleum and Petroleum Substitute Fuel Business Act.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea, Environmental Impact Assessment Division, with consultation from the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries for marine ecosystem impacts.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Vessel-only bunkering operations within an existing port berth or anchorage: Exempt from full EIA, but require an environmental registration and procedural review by the regional environmental authorities. Onshore fuel storage and bunkering infrastructure: Prior Environmental Review for aggregate tank capacity below the large-scale threshold; Full EIA may be required for new port water area development, dredging, or large tank farms in accordance with the Enforcement Decree of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Oily water discharge from machinery spaces must not exceed 15 ppm instantaneous oil content under MARPOL Annex I, regulation 15; zero oil discharge from bunkering operations into port waters. Fuel sulfur content used at berth in Korean port emission control areas must be 0.10% by mass or lower, and 0.50% by mass globally. Volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions from light product loading must be captured by vapor return or recovered through a vapor balance system. Hazardous petroleum waste must be tracked on the Korean electronic waste manifest system and transferred only to licensed treatment operators; storage areas must have secondary containment of at least 110% of the largest tank or container capacity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Completion Certificate and annual fire inspection under the Fire Prevention, Installation, Maintenance and Safety Management Act; Civil Defense emergency plan and incident command procedure approved by the local civil-defense authority and port control; structural load certification for piers, gangways, and loading arms; KOSHA occupational safety and health approval for harbor and marine-refueling workers under the Occupational Safety and Health Act including personal flotation devices, fall protection, and confined-space procedures; Korea Coast Guard oil spill response equipment approval required for bunkering operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea and its electronic portal HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr); Korea Customs Service (KCS) and its UNI-PASS electronic customs clearance portal (unipass.customs.go.kr) govern all export-side documentation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity must first appoint a domestic tax agent or establish a Korean place of business for Korean tax purposes. The entity then files an online business registration application through the NTS HomeTax portal with the competent district tax office. The submission package includes the foreign certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, evidence of the Korean place of business or valid tax agent appointment, authenticated signature or corporate seal documentation, identification of the responsible representative or agent, and any bunkering or maritime fuel supply statutory licence. The NTS issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN) that simultaneously serves as the VAT registration number; there is no separate VAT-only registration procedure. The same BRN must be used for electronic tax invoices, customs export declarations, VAT returns, foreign exchange reporting, and all indirect tax compliance communication with the NTS.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None; the Republic of Korea does not permit check-the-box pass-through elections for a Yuhan Hoesa. The entity is taxed as a separate juridical person under the Corporate Tax Act. A domestic group taxation election is available only for 100% locally owned subsidiaries that satisfy the statutory consolidation conditions, and no separate hybrid mismatch election is recognised.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Zero KRW threshold for juridical persons; a Korean-incorporated LLC must complete VAT registration before or upon starting business if it makes any taxable supply. The Korean VAT Act does not provide a general monetary registration exemption for juridical persons.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoicing is mandatory for all VAT invoice issuers. Every tax invoice must be created and transmitted through NTS HomeTax or an NTS-approved ASP/ERP channel, and must be delivered to the NTS by no later than the day after the date of issuance. Each transmitted electronic tax invoice receives a unique NTS approval number, creating a real-time anti-fraud clearance trail. No physical stamping or paper fiscal seal is used. B2C cash sales are separately reported through the NTS cash receipt system, and the NTS automatically cross-validates Business Registration Numbers, declared invoice amounts, VAT return data, and customs export declarations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available when goods are physically exported from Korea, evidenced by an accepted customs export declaration, and when the supply qualifies as an export supply under the Value-Added Tax Act. For marine bunkering and refuelling, the supply of bunker fuel, lubricants, and marine stores to a vessel engaged in international navigation or foreign trade qualifies for the 0% export VAT rate, provided the goods are delivered as stores for use on that vessel, are declared to customs as exports, and the export consideration is repatriated to Korea within the statutory deadline. Qualifying offshore services, including certain exported business-to-business digital and maritime auxiliary services performed outside Korea, are also zero-rated under the separate export-service provisions of the VAT Act.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration recorded and accepted in UNI-PASS (satisfying the Korean export declaration requirement)
Commercial invoice issued by the Yuhan Hoesa bunkering entity
Packing list for the bunker fuel or marine lubricant supply
Bill of Lading or sea waybill evidencing ocean carriage from Korea
Bunker Delivery Receipt / marine fuel delivery note signed by the vessel master or chief engineer and stating vessel name, IMO number, port of supply, and delivered volume
Bunker supply contract, voyage charter order, or purchase order
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC/FIRC) or Certificate of Export Proceeds Settlement issued by a Korean licensed foreign-exchange bank
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS will deny the 0% export VAT rate and reclassify the transaction as a taxable domestic supply if the required customs, transport, delivery, and inward-remittance documentation is not obtained and retained contemporaneously or if the foreign-currency export proceeds are not evidenced by a bank certificate within the statutory 180-day repatriation window. The denied VAT is assessed at 10% on the supply, together with statutory additional tax for underreporting or unreported tax, monthly overdue interest, and, in cases involving false or fraudulent export documentation, aggravated penalty tax and criminal exposure under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, including fines and imprisonment. Customs-side irregularities may also result in suspension of export-ledger privileges, denial of future zero-rated treatment, and penalties imposed by Korea Customs Service.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK), the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF), and the Korea Customs Service (KCS), with all foreign-exchange reporting executed through the Foreign Exchange Information Network (FEIN) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of Korea applies a substantially open current account regime but retains a managed floating capital account framework. Current account payments for goods, services, and ordinary trade settlement are freely convertible and can be executed through licensed foreign-exchange banks, requiring only accurate purpose-of-payment declarations and compliance with documentary rules. Capital account transactions such as equity injections, shareholder loans, and the issuance of foreign-currency debt are generally permitted for foreign investors but must be routed through an authorized foreign-exchange bank and reported to the Bank of Korea and the Ministry of Economy and Finance via FEIN. The Korean won is freely usable onshore for trading, but offshore KRW clearing is restricted and usually requires onshore bank participation; offshore NDF activity exists but onshore corporates must prove genuine trade exposure. Profit remittance is permitted through either the Foreign Investment Promotion Act or the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act regimes, provided that the initial foreign investment was properly registered and the remittance is supported by audited evidence of earnings. There is no mandatory percentage conversion of export proceeds into KRW; exporters may retain foreign currency in domestic foreign-exchange accounts, but all export proceeds must ultimately be repatriated and reported to Korean banking authorities within the statutory settlement window. The capital verification process is strict, requiring the bank to certify the actual receipt of foreign currency against a registered foreign investment declaration. Thus, while Korea is not a hard-currency-control jurisdiction, the MFEO and BOK impose rigorous transaction-level reporting, and any deviation from the declared purpose of a cross-border flow can trigger civil and criminal penalties under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds from general cargo shipped from South Korea must be repatriated to a licensed domestic foreign-exchange bank within two (2) years from the date of export declaration; for shipbuilding, offshore plant, heavy machinery, and manufacturing-intensive projects including marine bunkering vessels and fuel infrastructure, the statutory settlement window extends to five (5) years. The full invoice value must be received; however, the mandatory conversion ratio is zero percent, as Korea does not require conversion into KRW. Exporters may hold receipts indefinitely in an approved bank foreign-currency account, subject to quarterly FEIN reporting and supporting export documentation. If the buyer fails to remit within the permissible period, prior approval from the Ministry of Economy and Finance via the Bank of Korea is mandatory to avoid administrative fines.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Statutory non-viability for full treasury operations. Under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and the FSC licensing framework, no offshore fintech EMI or virtual-bank patchwork may open a KRW-denominated corporate account for a Korean resident entity or act as a settlement institution for capital account flows. Domestic e-money companies may only perform limited pass-through functions and cannot substitute for the licensed foreign-exchange bank required for FDI registration, capital verification, and trade payment reporting. Therefore, the Korea business must utilize a traditional tier-1 commercial bank; overseas EMIs are confined to supporting non-resident FX conversions outside regulated KRW clearing rails and may not be used for statutory import/export settlement or profit remittance reporting.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The statutory representative director is required to appear physically in-branch for the initial corporate account opening, along with the corporate seal certificate, certificate of business registration, passport/g-ivisa, Alien Registration Card (ARC), and board resolution approving the banking mandate. Korean banks uniformly reject fully remote onboarding for foreign directors and do not recognize a remote consular proxy opening as sufficient, except in narrow cases where a notarized and apostilled power of attorney is pre-cleared by the compliance chair, and even then a local corporate officer must attend a face-to-face interview. The director should anticipate a 45-60 minute enhanced due diligence interview, completion of tax information forms (Form W-8/W-9 equivalents), and signing of foreign-exchange confirmation declarations. A foreign-resident director who has registered an ARC may use a domestic branch representative with a specific notarized mandate, but most tier-1 banks still require the director to appear at least once for live identification under BOK AML requirements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity through nominee shareholders, bareboat charters, or layered foreign holding vehicles masking the true control of the vessel-bunkering operation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organisation chart from the shareholder registry through every intermediary to the ultimate beneficial owner; certified copies of passports of all individuals with 10 percent or greater ownership; apostilled certificate of incorporation for every holding entity; sworn beneficial ownership declaration; vessel charter registry extracts and AIS/IMO ownership record; monthly bank statements of each related vehicle.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctioned vessel, oil-major, or port exposure, particularly STS transfers at high-risk latitudes, AIS shadowing, or any trade involving flags of convenience with links to UN/OFSL/OFAC- and EU-listed ships.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full commercial invoice and stem contract identifying barge and receiving vessel IMO numbers; continuous AIS track reports for both vessels; independent ship-vetting report from a major P&I club; sanctions screening reports across OFAC/EU/UN and Korean MSIT/NIS lists; vessel flag certificate and P&I insurance certificate; bunker delivery receipt; customs pre-lodgement confirmation from the Korea Customs Service.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between declared bunker quantities and actual fuel loads on vessel voyages, suggesting under-invoicing, round-tripping, or trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent quantity surveyor report issued by SGS, Inspectorate, or CB&I for every stem; certified barge flow-meter calibration reports; sealed draught survey log; photograph of BDN signature; cargo manifest; bill of lading for ancillary marine fuel purchases; port authority clearance documents; invoice matching against prevailing Platts/Argus benchmark pricing for the fuel grade.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual incoming funding from third countries with inequitable link to the bunkering trade, including structured investments routed through low-tax territories and unexplained large capital injections.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-funds report for all non-trade payments; audited financial statements of the investor; corporate tax returns and capital verification certificate from the foreign exchange bank; FEIN FDI registration receipt; bank reference letters from EU/Asian banking relationships; sworn affidavit explaining the liquidity path from investor to Yuhan Hoesa Korean bank account; legal opinion from a reputable Korean law firm confirming the FDI structure.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity capital must be injected via a licensed foreign-exchange bank using a SWIFT MT103 wire from the overseas corporate bank account. The remitter must use the foreign direct investment (FDI) declaration approved by the Korean Foreign Exchange Bank and filed with the Bank of Korea through FEIN. The payment purpose code should reflect equity subscription/foreign investment capital; after receipt, the bank must issue a foreign-capital deposit certificate that serves as the capital verification record on which the Ministry of Justice, the tax authority, and the corporate registry rely. The funds must remain in the designated capital escrow account until verification is completed. The investor must obtain the foreign investment certificate from the KOTRA/KEB window before the inflow, and the remitting bank instruction must include the full investor legal name, Yuhan Hoesa entity ID, and the FDI registration number to avoid purposes mismatches. Once verified, the capital can be transferred to the operational KRW/USD settlement account at the same tier-1 bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rails for marine bunker fuel purchases and port disbursements are SWIFT MT103 for direct vendor payments and commercial documentary LCs (MT700) for larger ship-fuel supply contracts where the counterparty requires bank-issued payment security. For standby obligations and performance bonds to ports, shipyards, or charterers, a Standby LC (MT760) under UCP600/URDG758 is permissible. Korean banks also process documentary collections for cargo documents against acceptance or payment, but for fast-turnaround bunkering stems MT103 direct payments are preferred. All outbound payments must be tagged with correct FEIN trade purpose codes and supported by the BDN, vessel clearance, and customs records for each refueling event. For KRW disbursements to domestic ports and suppliers, the Korea Financial Telecommunications & Clearings Institute wires (BOK-Wire+) are used, while cross-currency transactions settle through the CLS or standard correspondent chains.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable KRW/USD FX forwards for trade receivables and payables with real underlying bunkering exposure
KRW/USD FX swaps for matching short-term current account cash-flow waterlines and managing liquidity tranches
Interest rate swaps denominated in USD or KRW for the long-term capital escrow financing, subject to genuine hedge treaty
Currency options and collar structures for hedging projected bunker fuel procurement costs when executed onshore with a licensed bank

Offshore NDF contracts for non-resident counterparties only; Korean-resident Yuhan Hoesa is generally restricted to onshore deliverable hedging instruments for transactions with Korean bank counterparts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (법인세 신고서) - annual corporation tax declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 in the year following the fiscal year-end; where the fiscal year coincides with the calendar year, the return and full payment become due on the last day of the third month after the end of the tax year (advance payments are due at the end of the 6th and 12th tax months)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surtax under the Framework Act on National Taxes: 20% of the tax underpaid; unpaid tax carries daily delinquency interest of 0.022% (about 8.03% per annum) from the statutory due date to the payment date; deliberate non-filing is subject to criminal prosecution under the Tax Crimes Penalty Act and the NTS may issue a compulsory collection order; no direct administrative strike-off by the NTS, but persistent non-filing for 3 consecutive years combined with non-registration of annual settlement enables the court registry to commence an administrative dissolution proceeding at the tax authority's request.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Local Income Tax Return (법인지방소득세 신고서) - local corporate surtax declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government revenue authority of the Si/Gun/Gu in which the registered office is located
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: April 30 following the end of the fiscal year (i.e., within four months after the fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surtax of 10% of the underpaid local income tax; daily overdue interest of 0.022% (8.03% per annum) on arrears under the Local Tax Collection Act; repeated non-compliance allows the local government to issue a demand notice, attach bank accounts and, if the company is inactive, apply to the district court for administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements Registration (정기 결산서류 등기) - filing of balance sheet, statement of income, and members' resolution approving the annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Office (등기소) of the District Court having jurisdiction over the company's registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days after the annual meeting of members approving the accounts; the meeting must be convened no later than the end of the sixth month after the fiscal year-end, making the last effective filing date July 14 for a December 31 fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file is subject to a court administrative fine of up to KRW 5 million (approximately USD 3,800); a company that remains in continued default for three consecutive years may be declared a dormant company and, after the court's peremptory notice and 14-day cure period, be struck off the commercial register upon application of any interested party or the public prosecutor.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Bunkering Business Operation Report / Licence Revalidation Report (선박급유업 사업보고서) for marine fuel supply and lubricant replenishment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Regional Maritime Affairs Office of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, or the city/province licensing bureau, depending on the integrated petroleum and marine-fuels licensing regime
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 31 of every year immediately following the licence anniversary; for licences issued as of July 1, an interim report is also due within 30 days of the anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late submission triggers a KRW 2 million (approximately USD 1,500) administrative fine under the Petroleum and Alternative Fuel Business Act; failure to maintain a valid bunkering licence while supplying marine fuel is punishable by imprisonment up to 3 years or a fine up to KRW 50 million (approximately USD 38,000); the maritime regulator may suspend the licence for up to 6 months and, for repeated violations, revoke it, after which the company can no longer lawfully operate and is exposed to court-ordered striking-off for carrying on a regulated activity without a licence.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit and Accounting (Act No. 18429, last amended 2023) and its Enforcement Decree, an independent certified public accountant audit is mandatory for a Yuhan Hoesa that: (a) is a listed issuer under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act; or (b) as of the close of the fiscal year has total assets of at least KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.0 million); or (c) reports total annual revenue of at least KRW 100 billion (approximately USD 75 million); or (d) employs, on average, at least 1,000 permanent employees; or (e) is within a conglomerate group that is required to file consolidated financial statements under K-IFRS. A Korean court may also order an external audit upon the request of any member or creditor even when the thresholds are not met, and members holding at least 5% of total capital may demand a special audit under the Commercial Act. All mandatory audits must be performed by an independent certified public accountant registered with the Securities and Futures Commission of the Financial Services Commission.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) as adopted by the Korean Accounting Standards Board for companies required to present IFRS financial statements; Korean GAAP for non-public companies; and the Korean SME Accounting Standards for eligible small corporations. Audit opinions and independent auditor's reports are issued in accordance with the Korean Standards on Auditing. Financial statements must be prepared on an accrual basis and presented consistently, with comparative prior-year figures.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Republic of Korea does not impose a separate annual beneficial-ownership filing on a private Yuhan Hoesa. Instead, the company has a continuous statutory duty to maintain an updated register of members and directors and to file a registry change application with the competent District Court commercial registry within 14 days of any change in members, shareholding percentages, directors, or registered office. For foreign-invested members, any change in shareholding that affects foreign-invested status must be reported to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy through the Invest Korea portal within 30 days. The statutory registers must be physically present at or accessible from the registered office, must be available for inspection by members during ordinary business hours, and must be presented to the certifying CPA during each annual compliance and audit review.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 - 4,000 per annum for a registered office, agent, and statutory register custody service in Korea; lower end for office-rental-only arrangements and higher end when corporate secretarial support is bundled with a local compliance consultancy.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 12,000 - 35,000 per annum for a full Korean certified CPA audit (K-IFRS / K-GAAP) of a bunkering LLC with marine fuel supply transactions; USD 6,000 - 15,000 if the company qualifies for the SME financial-statement review exemption and only a CPA review, corporate securities compliance review, and tax-side reconciliation are needed.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax on taxable income above KRW 300 billion, with lower brackets of 9%, 19%, and 21%; a local income tax surcharge equal to 10% of national corporate income tax applies, producing a top all-in marginal rate of 26.4%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Free Economic Zone and Free Trade Zone foreign-invested enterprises may qualify for statutory corporate income tax holidays: 100% exemption for the first 3 years and 50% reduction for the following 2 years, subject to the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and the Restriction of Special Taxation Act. General R&D tax credits and facility investment credits are available; Korea does not operate a patent box regime.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean Corporation Tax Final Return (Form 1 Corporate Tax Base and Tax Calculation Statement) with attached schedules for foreign tax credit, international related-party transactions, and non-resident withholding; filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return with a semi-annual interim prepayment return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; a December 31 fiscal-year filer must file by March 31. Interim prepayment returns are due within 2 months after the first six months of the fiscal year, which is August 31 for calendar-year taxpayers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Taxpayer Identification and Filing Status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business registration number, entity name, head office address, date of incorporation, principal business code (ISIC 5222 marine bunkering), and foreign-invested enterprise status under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all non-resident shareholders and their shareholding percentages. Attach the foreign-investment report, foreign investor Tax Residency Certificate (TRC), and beneficial ownership details when treaty relief will be claimed on outbound dividend payments. Misstating the non-resident ownership structure triggers withholding penalty risk.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Revenue, Cost of Sales, and Gross Profit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total sales revenue from ship fuel and lubricant replenishment, related costs of goods sold, and gross profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Bunker sale invoices must capture full volumetric and pricing data, including deliveries to foreign-flag vessels, storage locations, and vessel identities. If sales are invoiced through an offshore intermediary, the Korean entity must prove it is the principal performing the economic functions; circular offshore arrangements without substance will be recharacterized by the tax authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Worldwide taxable income calculated from financial income after Korean tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-deductible entertainment expenses, excessive intercompany interest exceeding thin capitalization limits, and non-arm's-length royalties paid to non-resident related parties. Deduct only statutory tax loss carryforwards within the 10-year limitation. Any dividend income from foreign subsidiaries must be properly characterized and supported by exemption/credit schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4a - Foreign Tax Credit and Foreign Income Exemption
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source income, foreign taxes paid on that income, and the foreign tax credit limited to Korean corporate income tax attributable to the foreign-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This box is used by the Korean entity, not by non-resident shareholders. Claim credits using tax-authority-certified foreign tax receipts with certified Korean translations; unsupported foreign tax credits will be rejected and converted into underpayment surcharges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate value of goods, services, intangibles, and financing transactions with foreign related parties, including bunker procurement from overseas affiliates and fuel sales to related shipping lines.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When aggregate related-party cross-border transactions reach KRW 10 billion per fiscal year, Master File and Local File transfer-pricing documentation must be maintained and produced on request. Provide a functional analysis, tested-party selection, arm's-length method, and comparability evidence. Non-disclosure exposes the entity to a transfer-pricing adjustment plus 20-40% surcharges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 - Withholding Tax on Payments to Non-Residents
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividends, interest, royalties, and other Korean-source income paid to non-resident payees and the withholding tax remitted to the National Tax Service.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Statutory aggregate withholding on non-resident dividends, interest, and royalties is 22% (20% national plus 2% local surtax). To apply a treaty reduction, file the non-resident treaty exemption/reduction application with the withholding agent before or at the time of payment, attach the TRC and beneficial ownership declaration, and retain full supporting records. Failure to withhold creates joint personal liability for the responsible director.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or negligent non-filing and under-reporting add surcharges of 20% of the unpaid tax; fraudulent omission or evasion adds 40%. Late payment carries a daily overdue surcharge under the Framework Act on National Taxes. Willful tax evasion is referred under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, with imprisonment of up to 3 years, increasing to 5 years where evaded tax exceeds KRW 300 million, and a fine of up to 3 times the tax evaded; non-filing of international transaction schedules additionally triggers independent penalty provisions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate outbound dividend withholding (20% national withholding plus 2% local income tax surcharge) on distributions to non-resident shareholders; applicable bilateral DTA rates commonly reduce this to 5-15%, with lower rates available for qualifying substantial shareholdings.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Korean withholding agent applies treaty relief after the non-resident recipient files an Application for Exemption from or Reduction of Non-Resident Withholding Tax under a Tax Treaty through HomeTax. Mandatory supporting evidence includes the Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the residence-state tax authority, a beneficial ownership declaration, shareholder register evidence, and substance documentation proving principal-purpose test compliance. The National Tax Service will deny relief if the recipient is a conduit shell without real economic substance, and will impose the full 22% statutory withholding plus penalties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory aggregate withholding is 22% for both interest and royalties (20% national plus 2% local surtax). Treaty rates commonly reduce interest to 0-15% and royalties to 0-15%, frequently 10%. Interest paid to foreign related lenders is limited by Korean thin capitalization rules of 3:1 debt-to-equity for general companies (6:1 for financial institutions); royalties must be arm's length, supported by actual IP ownership, and economically connected to the Korean business activity.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion aggregate annual cross-border related-party transactions triggers mandatory Master File and Local File preparation and production within 45 days of a National Tax Service request; Country-by-Country Report filing triggers at KRW 1 trillion consolidated group revenue.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not impose UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations on ordinary Korean bunkering companies, but economic substance remains a dispositive tax issue. Korean corporate residence is determined by the place of head office and effective management; treaty relief requires beneficial ownership and satisfaction of the principal-purpose test; and for a marine bunkering entity, the core income-generating activities (CIGA)—fuel procurement, storage, physical bunker delivery, invoicing, and treasury decisions—must be performed and documented in Korea. Artificial offshore arrangements, non-resident shell shareholders, and substance-less intermediary companies are vulnerable to GAAR, CFC attribution, treaty denial, and recharacterization of the entire transaction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Marine Fuel Tax Evasion / False Invoicing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Under-reporting taxable sales by omitting cash bunker receipts, inflating fuel losses, creating fake supplier invoices to reduce Korean corporate income tax and VAT, or mischaracterizing domestic deliveries to foreign-flag vessels as tax-exempt international sales without legal export documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 9: imprisonment not exceeding 3 years, or 5 years where the evaded tax exceeds KRW 300 million, and a fine not exceeding 3 times the tax evaded. The Framework Act on National Taxes adds 20% negligence and 40% fraudulent under-reporting surcharges, daily overdue surcharges, and VAT false-invoice penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for damages to the state under Korean Commercial Act Article 401. The National Tax Collection Act Article 12 permits secondary collection against directors who transferred or concealed company assets; the National Tax Service may blacklist the director and impose an overseas travel ban once unpaid taxes exceed KRW 30 million; the decision-maker faces criminal imprisonment, personal fines, and seizure of personal assets.
